children: Polish President Karol Nawrocki will again seek Prime Minister Donald Tusk's approval for the appointment of four members of the National Bank of Poland's management board after an earlier attempt failed to secure government backing.

In February, acting at the request of the NBP governor, Nawrocki nominated former NBP First Deputy Governor Marta Kightley and current MPC members Ludwik Kotecki, Przemyslaw Litwiniuk and Marcin Zarzecki to the management board.
However, the motion did not receive the legally required countersignature from Prime Minister Donald Tusk.

The government has not provided an explanation for why it blocked the appointments. Nawrocki and Tusk represent rival political groups, but the four candidates include two who were previously endorsed by Tusk's governing coalition.

"The President will once again submit the decision to the Prime Minister, requesting a countersignature for the appointment of four members of the National Bank of Poland management board," said the head of the President’s Office Pawel Szefernaker.
"He will propose the same candidates who were nominated by consensus in February," he said during a press conference.
According to the law, the management board consists of the governor and six to eight other members, each serving a six-year term. It currently has seven members, including the governor.

The term of office of one of the management board members expires in November 2026. Unless another member is elected to replace him, the NBP management board will consist of fewer members than required by law.
